feature: Ask's live line names each step as the plan is written
summary: While Ask writes a long plan, the line under the request now counts the steps and names the one it is on and the part it has reached ("Writing step 4: Radio, Dot"), instead of sitting on "Writing the steps". On a component sheet it never went more than 3.4 s without changing while writing (bar: 8 s).
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Ask's built-in model (Qwen3.8 27B on this Mac). Walk: Scripts/playtest/ask-names-each-step-as-it-writes-walk.json.

try.do: Open a blank picture and press Command-K.
Type: create a table of apple like quality base components that show different states and text, then press Return.
Watch the line under the request once it stops saying Reading your request: it counts the steps and names each part.
Let it finish and compare the sheet with one you made before today.
Open a new blank picture, press Command-K and ask: draw an illustration of a fox.

evaluate: Can you tell how far along a long plan is from the line alone?
Do the names it shows (Toggle, Knob, Disabled) read as the things you will see on the canvas?
Does the line change too often to read, or about right?
Is the finished sheet as good as before?
rough: Measured, component sheet (run 2, after the fixes): writing ran from 10.0 s to 117.7 s, 11 steps, 96 changes of line, longest without a change 3.4 s. The whole request's longest gap was 7.3 s, while the model read its second turn.

Measured, component sheet (run 1): writing ran 95 to 259 s and one step (Segmented Control) showed the same cut line for 22 s, since its long name pushed the part off the end. Fixed in this task: the name is now cut before the part, so each part shows (Writing step 6: Segmented…, Selection).
Measured, fox: the plan is one short step (Writing step 1: a fox, under a second); its longest gap is 4.0 s, during painting, as before. It still plans, paints, traces and checks the fox as it did.
The line changes about every 1.5 s while writing, so its fade between lines is often caught halfway (the first picture shows Message fading out as Success comes in).
Only the built-in model streams. With Ollama picked in Settings the line still says Writing the steps.
No mock draws this line's words; it keeps the panel's 40 character budget (UX-PATTERNS §4).
